sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K NATARAJAN  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K NATARAJAN)

This revision petition is filed by the petitioner- accused under Section 397 read with 401 of Cr.P.C., for setting aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the I-Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the First Appellate Court') in Crl. Appeal No.66/2015 dated 10.04.2019 by dismissing the appeal filed by the petitioner for having convicted the appellant by the II-Addl. Civil Judge &
JMFC, Kalaburagi in C.C.No.1732/2011 dated NC: 2024:KHC-K:6003 04.08.2015 for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 of IPC, wherein the Trial Court sentenced the appellant to undergo imprisonment for 2 years for the offence 498A, 6 months for the offence 323, 6 months for the offence 504 and 1 year for the offence 506 of IPC along with fine.
Aggrieved with the judgment of the concurrent findings of both the Courts below, the petitioner is before this Court.

2. During the pendency of this petition, the petitioner as well as the complainant who is wife of the accused examined as PW.1 appeared and filed joint compromise application under section 320(2) of Cr.P.C. seeking permission of the Court to compound the offence in I.A.No.1/2024.
3.
It is submitted by the both the complainant and petitioner that they are husband and wife.
There was matrimonial dispute between them.

The case was registered and they are living separately on Shanthkumar S/O Gunderao Biradar vs The State on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28011781/
2 the earlier occasion.

entities.text: Shanthkumar S/O Gunderao Biradar vs The State on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Later now they joined together and leading NC: 2024:KHC-K:6003 happy marital life and having two children.
Hence, prayed for permitting them to compound the offence.

4. I have perused the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by both the Courts below,
wherein the Trial Court based upon the evidence adduced by the prosecution almost nine witnesses and six documents and respondent-accused not lead any evidence.
Accordingly, after hearing arguments conviction and sentence was passed by the Trial Court.
The same was upheld by the First Appellate Court, which is under challenge.
5. The parties have submitted that they are compounded the offence and ready to live together.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hasi Mohan Barman and Another vs. State of Assam and another reported in (2008) 1 SCC 184, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has permitted to compound offence after judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the Sessions Court.

entities.text: Hasi Mohan Barman and Another vs. State of Assam and another reported in (2008) 1 SCC 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case previously there NC: 2024:KHC-K:6003 was no marriage between the parties at the time of commission of offence, subsequently after the conviction, the parties have compromised and lead happy marital life.
Considering the said facts and circumstances of the case the Hon'ble Supreme Court allowed the parties to compromise the case and reduced the sentence.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case though the complainant and petitioner joined together and living as husband and wife and leading happy marital life and in view of the above judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, I am of the view that the parties are permitted to compound the offence even in the appellate stage.

Accordingly I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The application in I.A.No.1/2024 is allowed.
Consequently, the revision petition is allowed.
ii. The judgment of conviction and sentence passed by II-Addl.

Civil Judge NC:
2024:KHC-K:6003 & JMFC, Kalaburagi in C.C.No.1732/2011 is set aside.

iii. The revision petitioner is acquitted for the charges leveled against him and his bail bonds,
if any, stands cancelled.
iv. The registry to send back the trial court records along with copy of this order to the Trial Court.

Sd/-
(K NATARAJAN) JUDGE SDU Ct:si Shanthkumar S/O Gunderao Biradar vs The State on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28011781/
